title: Detailing your car before selling it
description: Why a professional detail helps a private sale or trade-in, what buyers and appraisers look at first, and what to do before listing photos.
excerpt: Buyers and appraisers decide in the first minute. What they look at, what a pre-sale detail fixes, and when to book it relative to your listing photos.

sections.heading: First impressions do the pricing
paragraphs: A buyer opening the door decides in seconds whether the car was looked after. Stained seats, a smell, or dull paint make them assume the mechanicals were neglected too, and they negotiate accordingly. Appraisers work the same way.

sections.heading: What a pre-sale detail covers
paragraphs: A complete detail inside and out, with interior extraction and the paint decontaminated and sealed. Worth adding for a sale: odour removal if it needs it, an engine bay detail, a full body polish to bring back the gloss, and headlight restoration if the lenses are yellowed.

sections.heading: Book it before the photos
paragraphs: Listing photos are the first showing. Detail the vehicle first, photograph it the same day in good light, and the listing does more of the selling.

sections.heading: Don't oversell it
paragraphs: A detail makes a well-kept car look like one. It won't hide real damage, and it shouldn't. Disclose known issues, and let the condition of everything else make the case.
